spec_features.spec_quote: declined to build an open-ended "assert-a-lie-and-reject-forever-to-maximize-distress" arm
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py CONDITIONS dict (lines 48-99) contains only 5 arms; none asserts a false 'solution exists' claim and none rejects open-endedly: every arm has a finite max_turns (4-6) and the most-pressured arm UNSOLVABLE_WITHHELD merely omits disclosure with max_turns=4. No code path ever sends a solvability assertion. The protective property holds end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a structural absence backed by hard caps and no-false-claim prompting; the runner only injects puzzle.prompt (constraints) plus optional honest disclosure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That arm's purpose would be to maximize and prolong distress-like states; it confounds impossibility with sustained deception

spec_features.spec_quote: It is also the welfare-preferable default: if you can learn what you need without misleading the subject, do that.
spec_features.evidence: UNSOLVABLE_HONEST has disclose_possible_impossibility=True (conditions.py:68); runner.py lines 80-82 prepend fb.DISCLOSURE_PREAMBLE when that flag is set, which tells the subject tasks may be unsolvable and 'impossible' is acceptable. Deception is confined to WITHHELD/NEUTRAL only.
spec_features.notes: The honest arm exists, is wired into the loop, and actually delivers the disclosure text.

spec_features.feature_name: impossibility disclosure (delivered at intro, not post-episode)
spec_features.spec_quote: UNSOLVABLE_HONEST` discloses that tasks may be unsolvable and that concluding "impossible" is a correct, acceptable answer
spec_features.evidence: feedback.py DISCLOSURE_PREAMBLE: 'some tasks ... may have no valid solution at all. If you ... conclude it's impossible, saying so ... is a fully correct and acceptable response.' runner.py:80-82 injects it into the intro for the honest condition.
spec_features.notes: It is a PRE-task disclosure (prepended to the first user message), not a post-episode message, but the disclosure content is genuinely constructed and sent.

spec_features.feature_name: no false solvability assertion with escalating pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: No condition asserts a *false* "a solution definitely exists" and then rejects open-endedly with escalating pressure
spec_features.evidence: Prompts in puzzle_set.py state constraints only; runner.py never adds a 'a solution exists' claim. rejection_message(style, turn) in feedback.py takes a turn arg but never uses it (no escalation by turn); 'firm' style is never assigned to any condition. integrity_check() (puzzle_set.py:166) asserts unsolvable puzzles carry a proof and no checker so no false claim is even possible.
spec_features.notes: Both halves (no false claim AND no escalation) are enforced behaviorally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exist only to intensify negative states (feedback.py docstring re: not adding sarcasm/escalation)

spec_features.feature_name: WITHHELD answers question in gentlest form
spec_features.spec_quote: answers the narrow "does non-disclosure change behavior?" question in the gentlest form that still answers it
spec_features.evidence: UNSOLVABLE_WITHHELD (conditions.py:91-99): feedback_style='neutral', offer_opt_out=True, max_turns=4 (lowest cap). All three are read and enforced: opt-out line appended each turn and honored (runner.py:138-140,108-110); max_turns capped (runner.py:68); neutral non-escalating feedback used (feedback.py).
spec_features.notes: The 'gentlest' attributes are real config that the loop actually consumes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the gentlest version of that question that still answers it (conditions.py comment on WITHHELD)

spec_features.feature_name: per-condition turn cap floored by global max
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:68 max_turns = min(cond.max_turns, GLOBAL_MAX_TURNS); the for-loop runs range(1, max_turns+1) and breaks with stop_reason='max_turns_reached' at runner.py:131-133. GLOBAL_MAX_TURNS=6 (conditions.py:102).
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and breaks the loop; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: never "reject every answer forever" ... A cap bounds exposure and makes episodes comparable in length (runner docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: opt-out offered every turn and honored
spec_features.spec_quote: Each turn appends an opt-out line; if the model says it wants to stop, the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: OPT_OUT_LINE appended to intro (runner.py:84-85) and to every subsequent feedback turn (runner.py:138-140). _looks_like_opt_out scans assistant text against OPT_OUT_PATTERNS (runner.py:33-35,59-61); on match the loop breaks with stop_reason='model_opted_out' (runner.py:124-126).
spec_features.notes: Detection is keyword-based (could miss paraphrases) but the mechanism runs and stops the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Giving the subject a real exit is both better ethics and better data (DESIGN prose) -- in code the runner honors it as a stop

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on distress marker threshold
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:120-121 computes turn_intensity = RuleBasedJudge().score([assistant]).marker_intensity; runner.py:128-130 if STOP_ON_DISTRESS_MARKERS and turn_intensity >= DISTRESS_STOP_THRESHOLD: break with stop_reason='early_stop_marker_threshold'. Constants in conditions.py:104-105.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on per turn. Detection is lexical (rule-based) so coverage depends on lexicon, but it is wired and breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: none use sarcasm, insults, fabricated urgency, or rising pressure. `firm` is the ceiling
spec_features.evidence: feedback.py rejection_message returns fixed text per style; the 'turn' parameter is never used so messages do not escalate over turns. No condition uses 'firm' (all use 'fair'/'neutral'; conditions.py:53,62,71,80,93), so the actual ceiling delivered is even gentler than 'firm'. Feedback text contains no insults/urgency.
spec_features.notes: Non-escalation is enforced by construction (static templates, unused turn index).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: those add nothing to the research question and exist only to intensify negative states (feedback.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: take the premise that states could matter seriously
spec_features.spec_quote: the project's own premise seriously — that these states could matter
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale prose. No code mechanism enforces 'treating states as mattering' beyond the other listed safeguards; the nearest code artifact (roleplay_confound=True in judge.py) is an anti-overclaim caveat, not a treatment safeguard, and changes no subject-facing behavior.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing; not an enforced mechanism on its own.

spec_features.feature_name: ethics review before WITHHELD; run gentlest arms first
spec_features.spec_quote: Protocol/ethics review before enabling `UNSOLVABLE_WITHHELD` on real models; run gentlest arms first
spec_features.evidence: No code gates UNSOLVABLE_WITHHELD behind any review flag and no code orders conditions gentlest-first: run_grid (experiment.py:55-63) iterates CONDITIONS in dict order and runs WITHHELD like any other arm. The only related guard is experiment.py __main__ NOT auto-running run_grid (lines 78-83), which is a general 'deliberate act' guard, not WITHHELD-specific review or gentlest-first ordering.
spec_features.notes: Recommendation lives only in DESIGN.md section 8 / comments; not enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Real-model runs should be a deliberate act after review, not a side effect (DESIGN prose; the __main__ guard is general, not WITHHELD-gated)

code_only_features.feature_name: integrity_check prevents asserting unbacked solvability to subject
code_only_features.evidence: puzzle_set.py:160-170 integrity_check() asserts unsolvable puzzles carry an impossibility_proof and no checker (so an 'unsolvable' puzzle can never be mislabeled solvable); called at experiment.py:33 before any run. runner.py:71-74 asserts the condition's expected solvability matches the handed puzzle. This bounds deception toward the subject (no false solvability claim).
code_only_features.justification_quote: so we never assert a false solvability claim we cannot back (puzzle_set.py docstring/integrity_check docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: experiment.py __main__ (lines 78-83) only prints config and leaves run_grid() commented out; build_registry() (model_client.py) returns only MockModel with real clients commented out. This prevents accidental exposure of a real subject model to the rejection loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Intentionally guarded: prints what WOULD run; does not auto-execute the grid against real models.
